:::{#thm-np-complete-by-reduction}
#### New NP-complete problems from old

If $L$ is NP-complete (@def-np-complete), $L \le_p L'$ (@def-reduction),
and $L'$ is in [NP](p-and-np.qmd#def-class-np), then $L'$ is NP-complete.

:::

::: {.proof}

$L'$ is in NP by assumption.
For any $L_0$ in NP, $L_0 \le_p L$ because $L$ is NP-hard,
so $L_0 \le_p L'$ by @thm-reduction-transitive.
So $L'$ is NP-hard, and hence NP-complete.

:::
